sanskrit: mānavīṃ vṛṣabhāṃ caiva mahānadyo janādhipa sadānirāmayāṃ vṛtyāṃ mandagāṃ mandavāhinīm
english: The Mānavī and the Vṛṣabhā too, great rivers, O lord of men, the ever-wholesome Nirāmayā, the Vṛtyā, the Mandagā, and the slow-flowing Mandavāhinī.

sanskrit: brahmāṇīṃ ca mahāgaurīṃ durgām api ca bhārata citropalāṃ citrabarhāṃ mañjuṃ makaravāhinīm
english: The Brāhmaṇī and the great Gaurī, and the Durgā too, O Bhārata, the Citropalā, the Citrabarhā, the Mañju, and the Makaravāhinī.

sanskrit: mandākinīṃ vaitaraṇīṃ kokāṃ caiva mahānadīm śuktimatīm araṇyāṃ ca puṣpaveṇyutpalāvatīm
english: The Mandākinī, the Vaitaraṇī, and the Kokā, a great river, the Śuktimatī, the Araṇyā, the Puṣpaveṇī, and the Utpalāvatī.

sanskrit: lohityāṃ karatoyāṃ ca tathaiva vṛṣabhaṅginīm kumārīm ṛṣikulyāṃ ca brahmakulyāṃ ca bhārata
english: The Lohityā and the Karatoyā, and likewise the Vṛṣabhaṅginī, the Kumārī, the Ṛṣikulyā, and the Brahmakulyā too, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sarasvatīḥ supuṇyāś ca sarvā gaṅgāś ca māriṣa viśvasya mātaraḥ sarvāḥ sarvāś caiva mahābalāḥ
english: The most holy Sarasvatīs and all the Gaṅgās, O honored one — all of them mothers of the world, and all of them of mighty power.

sanskrit: tathā nadyas tv aprakāśāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ ity etāḥ sarito rājan samākhyātā yathāsmṛti
english: And rivers beyond reckoning besides, by the hundreds and the thousands. Thus, O king, have these streams been recounted, as memory serves.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ janapadān nibodha gadato mama tatreme kurupāñcālāḥ śālvamādreyajāṅgalāḥ
english: Now learn from me, as I declare them, the peoples that come next. There are the Kurus and Pāñcālas, the Śālvas, the Mādreyas, and the Jāṅgalas.

sanskrit: śūrasenāḥ kaliṅgāś ca bodhā maukās tathaiva ca matsyāḥ sukuṭyaḥ saubalyāḥ kuntalāḥ kāśikośalāḥ
english: The Śūrasenas and the Kaliṅgas, the Bodhas and the Maukas as well, the Matsyas, the Sukuṭyas, the Saubalyas, the Kuntalas, the Kāśis, and the Kosalas.

sanskrit: cedivatsāḥ karūṣāś ca bhojāḥ sindhupulindakāḥ uttamaujā daśārṇāś ca mekalāś cotkalaiḥ saha
english: The Cedis, the Vatsas, and the Karūṣas, the Bhojas, the Sindhus, and the Pulindakas, the Uttamaujas, the Daśārṇas, and the Mekalas together with the Utkalas.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ kauśijāś caiva ekapṛṣṭhā yugaṃdharāḥ saudhā madrā bhujiṅgāś ca kāśayo 'parakāśayaḥ
english: The Pāñcālas and the Kauśijas, the Ekapṛṣṭhas, the Yugaṃdharas, the Saudhas, the Madras, and the Bhujiṅgas, the Kāśis and the Aparakāśis.

sanskrit: jaṭharāḥ kukkuśāś caiva sudāśārṇāś ca bhārata kuntayo 'vantayaś caiva tathaivāparakuntayaḥ
english: The Jaṭharas and the Kukkuśas, and the Sudāśārṇas too, O Bhārata, the Kuntis and the Avantis, and the Aparakuntis as well.

sanskrit: govindā mandakāḥ ṣaṇḍā vidarbhānūpavāsikāḥ aśmakāḥ pāṃsurāṣṭrāś ca goparāṣṭrāḥ panītakāḥ
english: The Govindas, the Mandakas, the Ṣaṇḍas, the Vidarbhas, the Anūpavāsikas, the Aśmakas, the Pāṃsurāṣṭras, the Goparāṣṭras, and the Panītakas.

sanskrit: ādirāṣṭrāḥ sukuṭṭāś ca balirāṣṭraṃ ca kevalam vānarāsyāḥ pravāhāś ca vakrā vakrabhayāḥ śakāḥ
english: The Ādirāṣṭras and the Sukuṭṭas, and the Balirāṣṭra entire, the Vānarāsyas, the Pravāhas, the Vakras, the Vakrabhayas, and the Śakas.

sanskrit: videhakā māgadhāś ca suhmāś ca vijayās tathā aṅgā vaṅgāḥ kaliṅgāś ca yakṛllomāna eva ca
english: The Videhas and the Māgadhas, the Suhmas and the Vijayas likewise, the Aṅgas, the Vaṅgas, the Kaliṅgas, and the Yakṛllomans as well.

sanskrit: mallāḥ sudeṣṇāḥ prāhūtās tathā māhiṣakārṣikāḥ vāhīkā vāṭadhānāś ca ābhīrāḥ kālatoyakāḥ
english: The Mallas, the Sudeṣṇas, the Prāhūtas, and the Māhiṣas and Kārṣikas, the Vāhīkas, the Vāṭadhānas, the Ābhīras, and the Kālatoyakas.

sanskrit: aparandhrāś ca śūdrāś ca pahlavāś carmakhaṇḍikāḥ aṭavīśabarāś caiva marubhaumāś ca māriṣa
english: The Aparāndhras and the Śūdras, the Pahlavas and the Carmakhaṇḍikas, the Aṭavīśabaras too, and the dwellers of the desert lands, O honored one.

sanskrit: upāvṛścānupāvṛścasurāṣṭrāḥ kekayās tathā kuṭṭāparāntā dvaidheyāḥ kākṣāḥ sāmudraniṣkuṭāḥ
english: The Upāvṛts, the Anupāvṛts, the Surāṣṭras, and the Kekayas likewise, the Kuṭṭas, the Aparāntas, the Dvaidheyas, the Kākṣas, and the Sāmudraniṣkuṭas.

sanskrit: andhrāś ca bahavo rājann antargiryās tathaiva ca bahirgiryāṅgamaladā māgadhā mānavarjakāḥ
english: And the Andhras in great number, O king, and the Antargiris likewise, the Bahirgiris, the Aṅgas, the Maladas, the Māgadhas, and the Mānavarjakas.

sanskrit: mahyuttarāḥ prāvṛṣeyā bhārgavāś ca janādhipa puṇḍrā bhārgāḥ kirātāś ca sudoṣṇāḥ pramudās tathā
english: The Mahyuttaras, the Prāvṛṣeyas, and the Bhārgavas, O lord of men, the Puṇḍras, the Bhārgas, the Kirātas, the Sudoṣṇas, and the Pramudas likewise.

sanskrit: śakā niṣādā niṣadhās tathaivānartanairṛtāḥ dugūlāḥ pratimatsyāś ca kuśalāḥ kunaṭās tathā
english: The Śakas, the Niṣādas, the Niṣadhas, and likewise the Ānartas and the Nairṛtas, the Dugūlas, the Pratimatsyas, the Kuśalas, and the Kunaṭas as well.

sanskrit: tīragrāhās taratoyā rājikā rasyakāgaṇāḥ tilakāḥ pārasīkāś ca madhumantaḥ prakutsakāḥ
english: The Tīragrāhas, the Taratoyas, the Rājikas, the hosts of the Rasyakas, the Tilakas, the Pārasīkas, the Madhumantas, and the Prakutsakas.

sanskrit: kāśmīrāḥ sindhusauvīrā gāndhārā darśakās tathā abhīsārā kulūtāś ca śaivalā bāhlikās tathā
english: The Kāśmīras, the Sindhus and Sauvīras, the Gāndhāras, and the Darśakas likewise, the Abhīsāras, the Kulūtas, the Śaivalas, and the Bāhlīkas as well.

sanskrit: darvīkāḥ sakacā darvā vātajāmarathoragāḥ bahuvādyāś ca kauravya sudāmānaḥ sumallikāḥ
english: The Darvīkas with the Kacas, the Darvas, the Vātadhānas, the Amarathas, the Uragas, the Bahuvādyas too, O Kaurava, the Sudāmans, and the Sumallikas.

sanskrit: vadhrāḥ karīṣakāś cāpi kulindopatyakās tathā vanāyavo daśāpārśvā romāṇaḥ kuśabindavaḥ
english: The Vadhras and the Karīṣakas too, and the Kulindas of the foothills likewise, the Vanāyus, the Daśāpārśvas, the Romans, and the Kuśabindus.

sanskrit: kacchā gopālakacchāś ca lāṅgalāḥ paravallakāḥ kirātā barbarāḥ siddhā videhās tāmraliṅgakāḥ
english: The Kacchas and the Gopālakacchas, the Lāṅgalas, the Paravallakas, the Kirātas, the Barbaras, the Siddhas, the Videhas, and the Tāmraliṅgakas.

sanskrit: oṣṭrāḥ puṇḍrāḥ sasairandhrāḥ pārvatīyāś ca māriṣa athāpare janapadā dakṣiṇā bharatarṣabha
english: The Oṣṭras, the Puṇḍras, the Sairandhras as well, and the mountain peoples, O honored one. Now the other peoples, those of the south, O bull of the Bharatas:

sanskrit: draviḍāḥ keralāḥ prācyā bhūṣikā vanavāsinaḥ unnatyakā māhiṣakā vikalpā mūṣakās tathā
english: The Draviḍas, the Keralas, the Prācyas, the Bhūṣikas, the forest-dwellers, the Unnatyakas, the Māhiṣakas, the Vikalpas, and the Mūṣakas likewise.

sanskrit: karṇikāḥ kuntikāś caiva saudbhidā nalakālakāḥ kaukuṭṭakās tathā colāḥ koṅkaṇā mālavāṇakāḥ
english: The Karṇikas and the Kuntikas, the Saudbhidas, the Nalakālakas, the Kaukuṭṭakas as well, the Colas, the Koṅkaṇas, and the Mālavāṇakas.

sanskrit: samaṅgāḥ kopanāś caiva kukurāṅgadamāriṣāḥ dhvajiny utsavasaṃketās trigartāḥ sarvasenayaḥ
english: The Samaṅgas and the Kopanas, the Kukuras, the Aṅgadas, O honored one, the Dhvajinīs, the Utsavasaṃketas, the Trigartas, and the Sarvasenas.

sanskrit: tryaṅgāḥ kekarakāḥ proṣṭhāḥ parasaṃcarakās tathā tathaiva vindhyapulakāḥ pulindāḥ kalkalaiḥ saha
english: The Tryaṅgas, the Kekarakas, the Proṣṭhas, and the Parasaṃcarakas likewise, and the Vindhya tribes as well, the Pulindas together with the Kalkalas.

sanskrit: mālakā mallakāś caiva tathaivāparavartakāḥ kulindāḥ kulakāś caiva karaṇṭhāḥ kurakās tathā
english: The Mālakas and the Mallakas, and the Aparavartakas as well, the Kulindas and the Kulakas, the Karaṇṭhas, and the Kurakas likewise.

sanskrit: mūṣakā stanabālāś ca satiyaḥ pattipañjakāḥ ādidāyāḥ sirālāś ca stūbakā stanapās tathā
english: The Mūṣakas and the Stanabālas, the Satiyas, the Pattipañjakas, the Ādidāyas, the Sirālas, the Stūbakas, and the Stanapas as well.

sanskrit: hṛṣīvidarbhāḥ kāntīkās taṅgaṇāḥ parataṅgaṇāḥ uttarāś cāpare mlecchā janā bharatasattama
english: The Hṛṣīvidarbhas, the Kāntīkas, the Taṅgaṇas, the Parataṅgaṇas, and others, the barbarian peoples of the north, O best of the Bharatas:

sanskrit: yavanāś ca sakāmbojā dāruṇā mlecchajātayaḥ sakṣaddruhaḥ kuntalāś ca hūṇāḥ pāratakaiḥ saha
english: The Yavanas together with the Kāmbojas, savage barbarian tribes, the Kṣaddruhas, the Kuntalas, and the Hūṇas together with the Paratakas.

sanskrit: tathaiva maradhāś cīnās tathaiva daśamālikāḥ kṣatriyopaniveśāś ca vaiśyaśūdrakulāni ca
english: And likewise the Maradhas and the Cīnas, and the Daśamālikas as well, settlements of kṣatriyas, and families of vaiśyas and śūdras.

sanskrit: śūdrābhīrātha daradāḥ kāśmīrāḥ paśubhiḥ saha khaśikāś ca tukhārāś ca pallavā girigahvarāḥ
english: The Śūdras and Ābhīras, then the Daradas, the Kāśmīras together with their herds, the Khaśikas and the Tukhāras, the Pallavas, and the dwellers of the mountain caverns.

sanskrit: ātreyāḥ sabharadvājās tathaiva stanayoṣikāḥ aupakāś ca kaliṅgāś ca kirātānāṃ ca jātayaḥ
english: The Ātreyas with the Bharadvājas, and likewise the Stanayoṣikas, the Aupakas and the Kaliṅgas, and the tribes of the Kirātas.

sanskrit: tāmarā haṃsamārgāś ca tathaiva karabhañjakāḥ uddeśamātreṇa mayā deśāḥ saṃkīrtitāḥ prabho
english: The Tāmaras and the Haṃsamārgas, and likewise the Karabhañjakas. These lands have I named, O lord, only by way of brief mention.

sanskrit: yathāguṇabalaṃ cāpi trivargasya mahāphalam duhyed dhenuḥ kāmadhuk ca bhūmiḥ samyag anuṣṭhitā
english: And rightly tended, the earth yields, in measure of its quality and strength, the great fruit of the threefold aim of life, like a cow that gives milk, a cow that grants every wish.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ gṛdhyanti rājānaḥ śūrā dharmārthakovidāḥ te tyajanty āhave prāṇān rasāgṛddhās tarasvinaḥ
english: For her the kings are greedy, brave men skilled in dharma and gain; coveting her richness, those swift and strong ones lay down their very lives in battle.

sanskrit: devamānuṣakāyānāṃ kāmaṃ bhūmiḥ parāyaṇam anyonyasyāvalumpanti sārameyā ivāmiṣam
english: The earth is, beyond question, the refuge of the bodies of gods and men; and for her men prey upon one another, as dogs snatch at a piece of meat.

sanskrit: rājāno bharataśreṣṭha bhoktukāmā vasuṃdharām na cāpi tṛptiḥ kāmānāṃ vidyate ceha kasya cit
english: Kings, O best of the Bharatas, long to enjoy the earth that bears all wealth; yet here no man's desires are ever satisfied.

sanskrit: tasmāt parigrahe bhūmer yatante kurupāṇḍavāḥ sāmnā dānena bhedena daṇḍenaiva ca pārthiva
english: Therefore, O king, the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas strive to seize the earth — by conciliation, by gift, by sowing discord, and by force.

sanskrit: pitā mātā ca putraś ca khaṃ dyauś ca narapuṃgava bhūmir bhavati bhūtānāṃ samyag acchidradarśinī
english: Tended aright, the earth becomes father, mother, and son, sky and heaven to all living beings, O bull among men, looking upon them with a flawless eye.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca bhāratasyāsya varṣasya tathā haimavatasya ca pramāṇam āyuṣaḥ sūta phalaṃ cāpi śubhāśubham
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Of this land of Bhārata, and of Haimavata as well, O sūta, tell me the measure of the span of life, and its fruit, both fair and foul.

sanskrit: anāgatam atikrāntaṃ vartamānaṃ ca saṃjaya ācakṣva me vistareṇa harivarṣaṃ tathaiva ca
english: What is to come, what has passed, and what now is, O Saṃjaya — tell me of these at length, and of Harivarṣa as well.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca catvāri bhārate varṣe yugāni bharatarṣabha kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaṃ ca puṣyaṃ ca kuruvardhana
english: Saṃjaya said: In the land of Bhārata there are four ages, O bull of the Bharatas: the Kṛta, the Tretā, the Dvāpara, and the Puṣya, O increaser of the Kurus.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ kṛtayugaṃ nāma tatas tretāyugaṃ vibho saṃkṣepād dvāparasyātha tataḥ puṣyaṃ pravartate
english: First comes the age called Kṛta, then the Tretā age, O lord; thereafter, with the shortening of the Dvāpara, the Puṣya sets in.

sanskrit: catvāri ca sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ kurusattama āyuḥsaṃkhyā kṛtayuge saṃkhyātā rājasattama
english: Four thousand years, O best of the Kurus, is the reckoned span of life in the Kṛta age, O best of kings.

sanskrit: tathā trīṇi sahasrāṇi tretāyāṃ manujādhipa dvisahasraṃ dvāpare tu śate tiṣṭhati saṃprati
english: Three thousand in the Tretā, O ruler of men, two thousand in the Dvāpara; but now it stands at a mere hundred.

sanskrit: na pramāṇasthitir hy asti puṣye 'smin bharatarṣabha garbhasthāś ca mriyante 'tra tathā jātā mriyanti ca
english: In this Puṣya age there is no fixed measure of life at all, O bull of the Bharatas: here some die yet in the womb, and some die as soon as they are born.

sanskrit: mahābalā mahāsattvāḥ prajāguṇasamanvitāḥ ajāyanta kṛte rājan munayaḥ sutapodhanāḥ
english: In the Kṛta age, O king, men were born of great strength, great courage, and endowed with every excellence of progeny — sages rich in the wealth of austerity.

sanskrit: mahotsāhā mahātmāno dhārmikāḥ satyavādinaḥ jātāḥ kṛtayuge rājan dhaninaḥ priyadarśanāḥ
english: Of great zeal, great-souled, righteous, and truthful in speech — so were men born in the Kṛta age, O king, wealthy and fair to look upon.

sanskrit: āyuṣmanto mahāvīrā dhanurdharavarā yudhi jāyante kṣatriyāḥ śūrās tretāyāṃ cakravartinaḥ
english: Long-lived, of great valor, foremost among bowmen in battle — so are the kṣatriyas born in the Tretā: heroes and universal emperors.

sanskrit: sarvavarṇā mahārāja jāyante dvāpare sati mahotsāhā mahāvīryāḥ parasparavadhaiṣiṇaḥ
english: In the Dvāpara, O great king, men of all the orders are born, of great zeal and great might, yet bent upon the slaughter of one another.

sanskrit: tejasālpena saṃyuktāḥ krodhanāḥ puruṣā nṛpa lubdhāś cānṛtakāś caiva puṣye jāyanti bhārata
english: Endowed with but little luster, prone to wrath, greedy and given to falsehood — such are the men born in the Puṣya age, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: īrṣyā mānas tathā krodho māyāsūyā tathaiva ca puṣye bhavanti martyānāṃ rāgo lobhaś ca bhārata
english: Envy, pride, and wrath, deceit and spite as well, passion and greed — these arise among mortals in the Puṣya age, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: saṃkṣepo vartate rājan dvāpare 'smin narādhipa guṇottaraṃ haimavataṃ harivarṣaṃ tataḥ param
english: In this Dvāpara, O king, there is a dwindling, O ruler of men. Higher in excellence is Haimavata, and Harivarṣa higher still beyond that.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca jambūkhaṇḍas tvayā prokto yathāvad iha saṃjaya viṣkambham asya prabrūhi parimāṇaṃ ca tattvataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: You have duly described to me the Jambū continent, O Saṃjaya. Now tell me of its breadth and its extent, truly and exactly.

sanskrit: samudrasya pramāṇaṃ ca samyag acchidradarśana śākadvīpaṃ ca me brūhi kuśadvīpaṃ ca saṃjaya
english: And the measure of the ocean, O you of flawless sight; tell me too of the Śāka continent and the Kuśa continent, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: śālmalaṃ caiva tattvena krauñcadvīpaṃ tathaiva ca brūhi gāvalgaṇe sarvaṃ rāhoḥ somārkayos tathā
english: And truly of the Śālmala, and of the Krauñca continent as well; tell me all, O son of Gavalgaṇa, of Rāhu and of the Moon and the Sun.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rājan subahavo dvīpā yair idaṃ saṃtataṃ jagat sapta tv ahaṃ pravakṣyāmi candrādityau grahāṃs tathā
english: Saṃjaya said: O king, many indeed are the continents by which this world is spread out; but I shall declare to you the seven, and the Moon and Sun and planets as well.

sanskrit: aṣṭādaśa sahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ viśāṃ pate ṣaṭśatāni ca pūrṇāni viṣkambho jambuparvataḥ
english: Eighteen thousand yojanas, O lord of peoples, and six hundred full besides — such is the breadth of the Jambū mountain region.

sanskrit: lāvaṇasya samudrasya viṣkambho dviguṇaḥ smṛtaḥ nānājanapadākīrṇo maṇividrumacitritaḥ
english: The breadth of the Salt Ocean is reckoned twice as great, strewn with diverse peoples and bright with gems and coral.

sanskrit: naikadhātuvicitraiś ca parvatair upaśobhitaḥ siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇaḥ sāgaraḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ
english: Adorned with mountains gleaming with manifold minerals, thronged by Siddhas and Cāraṇas, the ocean lies girdling all around.

sanskrit: śākadvīpaṃ ca vakṣyāmi yathāvad iha pārthiva śṛṇu me tvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ bruvataḥ kurunandana
english: I shall now describe the Śāka continent duly, O king. Hear me as I speak of it in proper order, O delight of the Kurus.

sanskrit: jambūdvīpapramāṇena dviguṇaḥ sa narādhipa viṣkambheṇa mahārāja sāgaro 'pi vibhāgaśaḥ kṣīrodo bharataśreṣṭha yena saṃparivāritaḥ
english: By the measure of the Jambū continent it is twice as great in breadth, O ruler of men, O great king; and so too is the Sea of Milk in due proportion, O best of the Bharatas, by which it is encircled all about.

sanskrit: tatra puṇyā janapadā na tatra mriyate janaḥ kuta eva hi durbhikṣaṃ kṣamātejoyutā hi te
english: There the lands are holy, and there no man dies; how then could there be famine? For its people are endowed with patience and luster.

sanskrit: śākadvīpasya saṃkṣepo yathāvad bharatarṣabha ukta eṣa mahārāja kim anyac chrotum icchasi
english: This, O bull of the Bharatas, is a brief account of the Śāka continent, duly given, O great king. What else do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca śākadvīpasya saṃkṣepo yathāvad iha saṃjaya uktas tvayā mahābhāga vistaraṃ brūhi tattvataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: You have duly given me a brief account of the Śāka continent, O Saṃjaya, O greatly blessed one. Now tell me of it in full and exactly.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tathaiva parvatā rājan saptātra maṇibhūṣitāḥ ratnākarās tathā nadyas teṣāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu atīvaguṇavat sarvaṃ tatra puṇyaṃ janādhipa
english: Saṃjaya said: There too, O king, are seven mountains adorned with gems, and rivers that are mines of jewels — hear from me their names. All there is supremely rich in excellence and holy, O lord of men.

sanskrit: devarṣigandharvayutaḥ paramo merur ucyate prāgāyato mahārāja malayo nāma parvataḥ yato meghāḥ pravartante prabhavanti ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Frequented by gods, sages, and Gandharvas, the supreme one is called Meru; and stretching to the east, O great king, is the mountain named Malaya, from which the clouds arise and spread forth on every side.

sanskrit: tataḥ pareṇa kauravya jaladhāro mahāgiriḥ yatra nityam upādatte vāsavaḥ paramaṃ jalam yato varṣaṃ prabhavati varṣākāle janeśvara
english: Beyond that, O Kaurava, is the great mountain Jaladhāra, where Vāsava ever draws up the choicest waters, whence rain springs forth in the season of rains, O lord of men.

sanskrit: uccair girī raivatako yatra nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ revatī divi nakṣatraṃ pitāmahakṛto vidhiḥ
english: Lofty is the mountain Raivataka, where the constellation Revatī is ever fixed in the sky — so was it ordained by the Grandsire.

sanskrit: uttareṇa tu rājendra śyāmo nāma mahāgiriḥ yataḥ śyāmatvam āpannāḥ prajā janapadeśvara
english: And to the north, O king of kings, is the great mountain named Śyāma, from which the people have come to be dark of hue, O lord of the realms.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sumahān saṃśayo me 'dya proktaṃ saṃjaya yat tvayā prajāḥ kathaṃ sūtaputra saṃprāptāḥ śyāmatām iha
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A great doubt is mine this day at what you have said, O Saṃjaya. How, O son of the sūta, have the people there come to be dark of hue?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sarveṣv eva mahāprājña dvīpeṣu kurunandana gauraḥ kṛṣṇaś ca varṇau dvau tayor varṇāntaraṃ nṛpa
english: Saṃjaya said: In all the continents alike, O greatly wise one, O delight of the Kurus, there are two colors, fair and dark; and between the two, O king, lie all the other hues.

sanskrit: śyāmo yasmāt pravṛtto vai tat te vakṣyāmi bhārata āste 'tra bhagavān kṛṣṇas tat kāntyā śyāmatāṃ gataḥ
english: From what the darkness has arisen I shall tell you, O Bhārata: the blessed Kṛṣṇa abides there, and by his radiance the people have taken on a dusky hue.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraṃ kauravendra durgaśailo mahodayaḥ kesarī kesarayuto yato vātaḥ pravāyati
english: Beyond that, O lord of the Kurus, is the mighty mountain Durgaśaila of great glory, the Kesarin clothed in fragrant blooms, from which the wind blows forth.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yojanaviṣkambho dviguṇaḥ pravibhāgaśaḥ varṣāṇi teṣu kauravya saṃproktāni manīṣibhiḥ
english: The breadth of these in yojanas is twice as great, region by region; and the lands within them, O Kaurava, have been declared by the wise.
